rv.q: O’Neill’s play effectively strips back the political rhetoric and examines the personal reasons that drive people to violence.
One thing is certain, THE KELLY GIRLS will definitely leave a mark.
This is a rough, intimate play, set in a tiny seventy-seat storefront theater.
Shannon O’Neill’s world premiere play, The Kelly Girls, now on stage at the Factory Theater, is inspired by the real-life story of two other sisters who committed their lives to that fight.
Those worries quickly were put to rest as O’Neill’s work came to life with a bang, and unfolded with a gradual brilliance culminating as an undeniably magnificent, intimate drama.
Commanding performances by Amber Washington, Brittney Brown, and Ann Sheridan Smith make the Factory Theater’s world premiere production of “The Kelly Girls” a standout.

cn.t: Critics praise "The Kelly Girls" for its commanding performances and thought-provoking exploration of the Troubles in Northern Ireland, with the cast bringing depth and power to this politically charged family drama about radicalization and revolution.
